Championship leader Kimi Antonelli qualified seventh at his home race but is set to start near the back because of his engine penalty, while Lando Norris was left eighth after missing out on a helpful slipstream from McLaren team-mate Piastri.

items.originalTitle: 奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里谈2025年蒙扎车队指令："我不会改变我的回应方式"
items.summaryEn: A year ago, Oscar Piastri arrived at Monza as the title favourite, but his form declined from that weekend onwards and he ultimately lost the championship. Piastri says he would not change how he responded to the 2025 Monza team orders.
detailZh: 皮亚斯特里 谈 2025 年蒙扎的车队指令：“我不会改变我的回应方式”
Piastri 表示，对于在那场比赛中服从车队指令毫不后悔——那场比赛标志着他 2025 年状态下滑的开始
诺里斯，迈凯伦；皮亚斯特里，迈凯伦
整整一年前，皮亚斯特里 以夺冠热门的身份来到蒙扎，在队友 诺里斯 于赞德沃特退赛后，他以 34 分的优势领先对方——但正是从那个周末开始，情况开始出错。Piastri 最终失去了总冠军，赛季结束时仅位列第三，排在 Norris 之后，也排在 维斯塔潘 之后。
虽然几次糟糕的表现和失误让他损失了大量积分，但迈凯伦的一些决定也可能损害了这位澳大利亚车手的争冠之路。其中被讨论最多的一个决定发生在蒙扎，当时皮亚斯特里被要求在赛道上让诺里斯超越，因为这位英国车手进站时出现了慢速停站。
两人在那场比赛中一直在争夺第二名，诺里斯在大部分里程中处于领先——但他进站时出现的问题拖延了他的时间，实际上把这个位置拱手让给了皮亚斯特里。随后车队下达的车位交换指令，皮亚斯特里服从了，这一决定在围场内引发了关于车队是否给予诺里斯优待的争论。
当时车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉解释说，这一决定符合迈凯伦内部的“木瓜规则”，但仍有人认为皮亚斯特里不应服从这道指令。
兰多·诺里斯，迈凯伦；奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里，迈凯伦
在今年比赛开始前，排位赛后的新闻发布会上，皮亚斯特里被要求回顾那起事件，并在已知之后赛季如何展开的情况下，评估自己是否会改变任何做法。
这位澳大利亚车手回答说，他并不后悔。
“不，我的意思是，我不认为就是这一件事导致去年下半年变得艰难，”他说。“是每周一系列不同的因素，而且，你知道，你总是会想到本来可以做出不同的决定。
“但对我而言，就我如何回应、如何应对去年来说，我不会改变。所以，是的，没有什么要改变的。”
从那以后，皮亚斯特里（Piastri）仍未再赢得另一场F1比赛。在去年错失总冠军之后，他本赛季的表现也明显在速度上不及诺里斯（Norris）。
据信，这位澳大利亚车手目前遇到的许多问题都与他的驾驶风格有关，斯特拉（Stella）表示皮亚斯特里需要运用一些对他来说并非本能掌握的技术，因为他在低抓地力条件的赛道上也一直挣扎。随着2026年赛车产生的下压力更少，同样的模式似乎仍在延续。
皮亚斯特里本人表示事情并没有那么简单——但他相信自己正在开始释放更多速度，并强调了他在两周前赞德沃特排位赛中取得的进步。
“我是说，我认为这并不是某一个不断重复出现的问题，”他在蒙扎比赛周末前表示。“你知道的，我们总是在追寻一些稍微不同的东西。所以，我和我身边的团队都需要努力更快地找到它。”
“但我认为赞德沃特站的积极因素是，排位赛的表现至少看起来明显更好，恢复到了应有的水平。而且，你知道，我们正在经历的过程就是努力把这种状态延续到正赛中。”
“显然，赛车在正赛中的表现与单个飞驰圈相比有很大不同，但我感觉我们已经找到了一些相当不错的答案，解释了为什么赞德沃特站尤其具有挑战性。所以，是的，我认为我们在这方面取得了良好进展。我们只是需要时间和一些试验来找到能让我们更快的东西。但我有信心，我们正在找到正确的答案，找到前进的方向。”
在蒙扎站比赛之前，皮亚斯特里以104分位居车手积分榜第七，落后队友诺里斯55分，诺里斯以159分排名第四。
detailEn: Oscar Piastri on Monza 2025 team orders: "I wouldn’t change how I responded"
Piastri says he has no regrets about obeying team orders in the race which marked the start of his 2025 decline
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren

Exactly a year ago, Oscar Piastri arrived at Monza as the title favourite, leading team-mate Lando Norris by 34 points after the latter's retirement at Zandvoort - but it was from that weekend onwards that things started to go wrong. Piastri eventually lost the title, ending the season third behind not only Norris, but also Max Verstappen.

While several poor performances and mistakes cost him a significant number of points, some decisions from McLaren also potentially hurt the Australian's title bid. One of the most discussed came at Monza, when Piastri was asked to let Norris through on track after a slow pitstop for the Briton.

The duo had been battling for second in that race, with Norris ahead for most of the distance - but a problem during his pitstop delayed him and effectively cost him the position to Piastri. The subsequent order, which the Australian obeyed, sparked a debate in the paddock over whether the team was giving preferential treatment to Norris.
With team principal Andrea Stella explaining at the time how the decision was in line with McLaren's internal "papaya rules", some were still left feeling Piastri should not have obeyed the order.
Lando Norris, McLaren, Oscar Piastri, McLaren

Ahead of this year's race, at the post-qualifying press conference, Piastri was asked to look back at the incident and assess whether he would change anything, knowing how the season unfolded afterwards.
The Australian responded that he had no regrets.

"No, I mean, I don’t think it was, you know, one thing that led to the back end of last year being difficult," he said. "It was a number of different things week to week and, yeah, you know, you always think about different decisions you could have taken.
"But I think for me, how I responded, how I handled last year, I wouldn’t change it. So, yeah, nothing to change."
Piastri is still yet to win another F1 race since then. Having missed out on the title last year, he has also clearly lacked pace compared to Norris this season.

It is believed that many of the issues the Australian is experiencing now are related to his driving style, with Stella saying Piastri needs to deploy some techniques that don't come naturally to him, as he has also struggled at tracks with low-grip conditions. With the 2026 cars producing less downforce, the same pattern appears to have continued.
Piastri himself says it is not that simple - but believes he is starting to unlock more pace, highlighting the progress he made in qualifying at Zandvoort two weeks ago.

"I mean, I think it's not kind of one problem that keeps reoccurring," he said ahead of the Monza weekend. "It's, you know, kind of like we're always chasing something a little bit different. And yeah, we need to try and find it a bit quicker, both myself and the team around me.

"But I think the positive from Zandvoort was that the qualifying at least looked significantly better and back to the level it should be at. And, you know, the process we're going through is just trying to extend that to the races.

"Obviously, the car's quite different in a race compared to over a single lap, but I feel like we've got some pretty good answers of why Zandvoort particularly was challenging. So, yes, I think we're making good progress with that. We just need time and some experimentation to find, you know, to find some things that are going to make us quicker. But I'm confident that we're finding the right answers and finding a way forward."
Ahead of the Monza race, Piastri sits seventh in the championship on 104 points, 55 behind team-mate Norris, who is fourth on 159.

items.titleZh: 阿尔派蒙扎干地正面对决夺杆位，可媲美2012年马尔多纳多冷门
items.summaryZh: 阿尔派车手加斯利在意大利大奖赛干地排位赛中正面对决拿下杆位，这一表现极为罕见。The 比赛分析认为，原因一半在于阿尔派做对了，一半在于本应击败它的车队出现了失误。
items.originalTitle: 阿尔派在蒙扎做对了什么，而其他车队又做错了什么
items.summaryEn: Alpine, currently sixth in the constructors' championship, took pole position at the Italian Grand Prix in a straight fight in a dry qualifying session. The Race argues the result was a 50/50 split between what Alpine got right and what the teams that should have beaten it got wrong.
detailZh: 目前在一级方程式车队积分榜上排名第六的车队，刚刚在意大利大奖赛一场干燥条件下的排位赛正面较量中夺得了杆位。
F1赛场上常见的黑马杆位往往出现在混杂天气条件下，但皮埃尔·加斯利（加斯利）和阿尔派在蒙扎取得的成绩则完全不同。

要找到类似的先例，你得追溯到2012年西班牙大奖赛，当时帕斯托·马尔多纳多（Pastor Maldonado）为威廉姆斯车队（当时排名车队积分榜第七）夺得杆位——而且那次的成就还得益于刘易斯·汉密尔顿（汉密尔顿）的杆位赛车迈凯伦被取消了排位赛成绩。这样看来，真正可比的或许是2009年吉安卡洛·费斯切拉（Giancarlo Fisichella）为印度力量车队在比利时夺得的杆位（该车队在那场比赛之前赛季积分为零）。
答案其实是两方面的因素各占一半：一方面是阿尔派做对了的事情，另一方面是本应击败它的车队所犯下的错误。
梅赛德斯——更确切地说是乔治·拉塞尔，因为队友基米·安东内利将背负较大的发车罚退——以明显热门的身份进入排位赛，梅赛德斯的大多数对手都预计拉塞尔会拿到杆位。
第一次Q3飞驰圈之后局势也正是朝着这个方向发展，拉塞尔占据了临时杆位，他在发车直道上从安东内利那里获得了一点尾流帮助，而安东内利早已明确表示他愿意在Q3中牺牲自己来帮助拉塞尔。
但在关键的最后一圈准备阶段，一切都出了问题。拉塞尔在赛道上跟在安东内利后面，然而安东内利在帕拉博利卡弯遇到了正在减速的马克斯·维斯塔潘，不得不减速避让，结果堵到了拉塞尔，而拉塞尔也不得不在开始飞驰圈之前减速。
安东内利在发车直道上给拉塞尔做了尾流，然后在第一个减速弯前让开，结果拉塞尔从维斯塔潘那里得到了尾流，尽管距离比他想要的更近。拉塞尔称这有点像"一团糟"。
他在最后一节练习中仍然提升了自己的单圈时间，但最终落后加斯利0.060秒——这个差距很可能是由于准备不理想而损失的。此外，Russell的刹车锁死问题也困扰着他，就像蒙扎的许多车手一样。
Russell承认“这是一次非常混乱的练习赛”，并表示赛车的感觉不如最后一次自由练习时那么好。
毫无疑问，这仍然是一辆足以锁定杆位的赛车。把Russell三个最好的计时段组合起来，他的理想单圈是1分21.633秒，比他的排位赛圈速快0.233秒，比Gasly的杆位圈速快0.155秒。
相比之下，Gasly在最后一节把三个最好的计时段都组合到了一起。- Josh Suttill
汉密尔顿在排位赛后相当明确地表示，他觉得法拉利在调度两辆赛车的方式上本应更加协调。
如果你把阿尔派在三个节段中顺畅的运转——从Q1到Q3一直让加斯利排在成绩榜前列或接近顶端——与法拉利相对起伏不定的表现对比一下，就能理解汉密尔顿赛后为何如此沮丧。
要不是博托莱托的奥迪在Q2末段通过Ascari减速弯中段时转向过度，汉密尔顿甚至都进不了Q3，而法拉利（迈凯伦也是如此）为了把两辆赛车都推向发车区前排所冒的更大风险，相比阿尔派、梅赛德斯和红牛采取的“基本上牺牲一辆赛车”的策略，暴露得更加明显。
而且法拉利即便搭载了升级版ADUO 2引擎，在每一个测速点上仍然存在10-20公里/小时的差距，这说明执行得当的拖速和干净的飞圈对汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔的机会来说更加宝贵。
考虑到法拉利在Q2中差点酿成大祸，最终却（也算侥幸地）让两辆赛车都从第二排发车，对于这样一个混乱的排位赛来说，这是一个绝佳的结果。—— Ben Anderson
蒙扎从来不被认为是迈凯伦的主场，但MCL40在排位赛模式下的真实速度比预期更强——当然远好于其最终第六（皮亚斯特里）和第八（诺里斯）的发车位。
“说‘哦我们的阻力太大’其实有点像烟雾弹，或者说是借口。”车队领队Andrea Stella在谈到赛车空气动力学效率不佳所起的作用时说道。相反，他明确指出迈凯伦本应“有能力竞争前排头两排的位置”却表现不佳，问题出在执行层面。
隐藏在Q2中稳健的第二和第三名之下的，是第一个关键失误。Piastri在第一次出场时驶上赛道，恰逢节奏错乱的劳森正在做飞驰圈，导致他在减速弯阻碍了红牛赛车。结果Piastri被罚退三位发车，这将使他从第六位发车参加明天的正赛。
第三节排位赛（Q3）问题层出不穷。迈凯伦很难让自己的两辆车处于理想的尾流位置，部分原因在于其维修区的位置。这意味着诺里斯在Q3第一飞圈时没有得到好的尾流。第二飞圈时，两辆迈凯伦位于车群前方，皮亚斯特里在前，但当他锁死轮胎并切过第一个减速弯时，不仅妨碍了诺里斯，还让自己失去了牵引尾流。尽管诺里斯在那次飞圈中有所提升，但提升幅度远不及应有的水平。
皮亚斯特里的那次锁死，是没有通过妥善处理4MJ能量回收上限来优化出圈圈的结果——这个上限使得在飞圈开始前很难让所有部件都达到工作温度。除此之外，斯特拉承认：“我们在管理电池方面遇到了一些问题，而在蒙扎，电池电量每损失1%就会让你损失相当可观的毫秒数。”——Edd Straw
某种意义上说，红牛为阿尔派的杆位做出了最大贡献，因为维斯塔潘的位置安排影响了拉塞尔的那一圈，而拉塞尔本应凭借那一圈击败加斯利。
红牛本应很好地具备进行车队内部尾流配合的条件，因为劳森的罚退意味着他自己的成绩几乎可以被牺牲掉，用来为维斯塔潘提供助力。
不过前提是劳森(Lawson)得进入Q3。而很大程度上（但不完全是）由于皮亚斯特里(Piastri)在Q2中在维斯塔潘(Verstappen)正要给他回馈尾流时挡住了他，劳森实际上没能在需要他配合车队时出现在Q3。
但维斯塔潘认为，这些都不如那个未指明的部件故障重要——正是那个故障导致他的红牛赛车在Q3的飞驰圈中没能以正确的行驶高度运行。
“考虑到赛车在第三次自由练习中的表现，我以为我没法争夺杆位，但这次开起来难得地挺舒服，这其实感觉很好，”维斯塔潘说，“但不幸的是，我们在排位赛中又遇到了一个问题。”
这是他在排位仅列第六后通过电台咆哮“这车是纸做的”的外交辞令式翻译。——马特·比尔(Matt Beer)
可以公平地说，对于这个在意大利大奖赛周末之前做梦都没想到的杆位，阿尔派和它的对手们一样感到惊讶。
当它在周六晚上试图拼凑出自己是如何做到这一点的答案时，情况变得很清楚：尽管大车队们都以各自的方式出现了失误，阿尔派同样也通过把一切可控因素做到极致，让自己处于最佳位置来抓住机会。
在蒙扎拥有一台梅赛德斯引擎当然有帮助，因为它仍然是基准动力单元。
而阿尔派今年早些时候的一个弱点——下压力不足——在蒙扎很可能反而因低阻力优势变成了强项。
A526看起来非常高效，拥有不错的极速，这让它在竞争中脱颖而出。
Gasly在赞德沃特首次获得升级，也让赛车的平衡性更好，并且整个练习赛期间阿尔派不断完善调校，让他进入了非常满意的状态。
这让他能在刹车时攻击弯角（其他车手在这方面相当挣扎），并在Ascari弯和Parabolica弯把赛车推向极限。
不过最关键的也许是Gasly在一列车流中完美的尾流位置。
阿尔派有信心在最后一节跑到队尾——因为那样能获得最大的尾流收益。
这并非没有风险，因为前方慢车的威胁意味着你可能无法及时过线（Gasly和科拉平托以大约10秒的富余量赶上了），此外还存在前方任何人失控并引发黄旗从而打乱一切的危险。
尽管有几辆车在1号弯冲出了缓冲区，Gasly还是跑出了一趟干净的飞行圈，并借助前方Hamilton的美妙尾流，为自己争取到了百分之六秒的优势，从而超越Russell登顶。- Jon Noble
detailEn: The car that's currently sixth in the Formula 1 constructors' championship just took pole position in a straight fight in a dry qualifying session at the Italian Grand Prix.
F1 is used to freak underdog poles in mixed weather, but Pierre Gasly and Alpine's Monza achievement was something very different.

You have to go back to Pastor Maldonado's 2012 Spanish GP pole for Williams (then seventh in the championship) for an equivalent - and even that only happened because Lewis Hamilton's pole-winning McLaren was excluded from qualifying. Which means perhaps the real equivalent is Giancarlo Fisichella's 2009 Belgium pole for Force India (which was on zero points for the season before that race).
The answer is really a 50/50 split between things Alpine got right and things the teams that should've beaten it got wrong.

Mercedes, and more specifically George Russell given team-mate Kimi Antonelli had a sizeable grid penalty, went into qualifying as the clear favourite, with most of Mercedes' rivals expecting Russell to emerge with pole position.

And it was heading that way after the first Q3 run, with Russell on provisional pole, via a small tow assist on the start/finish straight from Antonelli, who had already made it clear he'd sacrifice his Q3 to help Russell.

But everything went wrong in the preparation for the crucial final lap. Russell was running on track behind Antonelli, however, Antonelli encountered a slowing Max Verstappen at Parabolica and had to back up into Russell, who also had to slow just before opening his flying lap.

Antonelli towed Russell on the start/finish straight, then jumped out of the way before the first chicane, leaving Russell to pick up a tow from Verstappen, albeit closer to him than he'd have liked. Russell called it a "bit of a mess".

He still improved his laptime on his final run, but he ended up 0.060s behind Gasly - time he likely lost with the sub-optimal preparation. Plus, Russell struggled with his brakes locking like many drivers at Monza.
Russell admitted "It was a very scrappy session" and said the car didn't feel as good as it did in final practice.

It was undoubtedly still a car good enough to secure pole position. Put together Russell's three best sectors and his ideal lap is a 1m21.633s, 0.233s faster than his qualifying lap and 0.155s ahead of Gasly's pole lap.
Gasly in contrast put all of his three best sectors together on his final run. - Josh Suttill
Hamilton made it fairly clear after qualifying that he felt Ferrari should have been much more coordinated in how it choreographed its two cars.

If you contrast how smoothly Alpine ran throughout the three segments, getting Gasly at or near the top of the timesheet from Q1 right through to Q3, with Ferrari's relatively yo-yo performance, you can understand why Hamilton was so frustrated afterwards.

But for Gabriel Bortoleto's Audi oversteering through the middle of the Ascari chicane at the end of Q2, Hamilton wouldn't have even made Q3, and the higher risks taken by Ferrari (and McLaren for that matter) in trying to work both cars towards the front of the grid were more exposed to the ‘essentially sacrifice one car' approaches taken by Alpine, Mercedes and Red Bull.

And the fact Ferrari, even with its updated ADUO 2 engine, still carried a 10-20km/h deficit through every speed trap, suggested properly executed towing and clean laps were even more valuable to Hamilton's and Charles Leclerc's chances.

Considering how close Ferrari came to disaster in Q2, to then have both its cars ultimately (and fortuitously) starting on the second row of the grid is a fantastic outcome from such a messy session. - Ben Anderson

Monza was never expected to be McLaren territory, but the underlying pace of the MCL40 in qualifying trim was stronger than expected - certainly far better than its final grid positions of sixth (Oscar Piastri) and eighth (Lando Norris).

"It would be a little bit of a red herring, or an excuse, to say 'oh we have too much drag," said team principal Andrea Stella of the role the car's aero efficiency weakness played. Instead, he pointed firmly in the direction of execution for McLaren's underachievement when it should have been "in the mix for the first couple of rows".

Hidden beneath a solid second and third in Q2 was the first key mistake. Piastri joined the track for his first run at the point where an out-of-synch Liam Lawson was on a quick lap, leading to him impeding the Red Bull in the chicane. A three-place grid penalty was the result, which puts Piastri sixth for tomorrow's race.

In Q3, there were myriad problems. McLaren struggled to position its cars ideally for a slipstream, which was partly owing to its position in the pitlane. This meant Norris didn't have a good slipstream on his first run in Q3. The McLarens were then at the front of the pack for the second run, with Piastri ahead, but when he locked up and cut the first chicane it not only hindered Norris but cost him his tow. Although Norris did improve on that run, it wasn't by anything like it should have been.

That lock-up from Piastri was a consequence of not optimising the outlaps by dealing well with the 4MJ harvest limit that makes it difficult to get temperature into everything before the start of a push lap. On top of that, Stella admitted that "we had some issues managing the battery, and here in Monza every 1% in the battery charge costs you a significant amount of milliseconds". - Edd Straw
In a way Red Bull made the biggest contribution to Alpine's pole given how much Verstappen's positioning affected the lap with which Russell really should've beaten Gasly.

And Red Bull should have been well placed to pull off some intra-team slipstreaming choreography given Lawson's grid penalties meant his own performance could be pretty much sacrificed to boost Verstappen.

Only if Lawson got to Q3, though. And thanks in large part (but not solely due) to Piastri baulking him in Q2 just as he was being given a reciprocal tow by Verstappen, Lawson wasn't actually there to play the team game when it was needed.
But Verstappen didn't think any of that mattered as much as the unspecified component failure that meant his Red Bull wasn't running at the right ride height for his Q3 runs.

"With how the car was responding in FP3, I didn't think I was fighting for pole, but it was quite a comfortable car to drive for once, and that was actually really nice," said Verstappen, "but unfortunately then we picked up another problem in qualifying."
Which was the diplomatic translation of his "this car is made of paper" radio rant after qualifying only sixth. - Matt Beer
It is fair to say that Alpine was as surprised as its rivals about a pole position that it had never even dreamed of before the Italian Grand Prix weekend.

As it tried to piece together the answers on Saturday night as to how it had done it, it became clear that, as much as the big teams had all slipped up in their own ways, Alpine had equally got itself into the perfect position to capitalise by getting everything within its control spot on.
Having a Mercedes engine around Monza certainly helped, as it remains the benchmark power unit.
But one of Alpine's weaknesses earlier in the year – of not enough downforce – may well also have become a strength at Monza because of the low drag benefit.
The A526 appears to be very efficient with good top speed, so that helped lift it into contention.
The upgrades Gasly first got for Zandvoort have also served to give the car a better balance, and throughout practice Alpine had evolved the set-up to get him into a place he was very happy with.
That allowed him to attack the corners under braking (where others were struggling a lot) and take things to the edge through Ascari and Parabolica.
Perhaps most critical of all though was Gasly's perfect slipstream positioning in the train of cars.
Alpine had confidence to drop to the back of the pack in that final run – as that offered the biggest tow gain.

That is not without risk, because there is a threat of slow traffic ahead meaning you don't get across the line in time (Gasly and Franco Colapinto made it with around 10 seconds to spare), plus a danger of anyone ahead going off and bringing out yellow flags that derail everything.

Despite a couple of cars going down the escape road at Turn 1, Gasly had a clear run and a beautiful slipstream from Hamilton ahead to secure himself the six-hundredths of a second edge that gave him the top spot over Russell. - Jon Noble

items.titleZh: 安东内利：我按车队要求为拉塞尔提供牵引，期待赛季后期获得回报
items.summaryZh: 在蒙扎排位赛中，基米·安东内利按车队要求帮助队友兼冠军竞争对手乔治·拉塞尔获得牵引，并期待对方在赛季后期以同样方式回报自己。

items.originalTitle: 安东内利：我按车队要求行事，期待拉塞尔赛季后期回报
items.summaryEn: Kimi Antonelli says he helped his team-mate and title rival George Russell with a tow during Monza qualifying as instructed by the team, and he expects Russell to return the favour later in the season.
detailZh: “我做了车队要求我做的事”：基米·安东内利预计乔治·拉塞尔将在本赛季晚些时候回报这份人情
由于发车罚位影响了他在蒙扎的比赛周末，基米·安东内利在排位赛中专注于帮助冠军竞争对手乔治·拉塞尔——并预计这份人情会在之后得到回报
乔治·拉塞尔（拉塞尔），梅赛德斯；安德烈亚·基米·安东内利（安东内利），梅赛德斯
在蒙扎排位赛中为乔治·拉塞尔提供尾流拖曳帮助之后，基米·安东内利表示，他预计自己的队友兼冠军竞争对手会在本赛季晚些时候以同样的方式回报他。
这位意大利车手由于背部发车区受罚，从自己的排位赛成绩中几乎得不到任何收益，实际上他在整个节里都是在帮助拉塞尔，后者最终获得第二。
梅赛德斯借此机会在蒙扎为安东内利的赛车安装了新的发动机部件，因为这是赛历中最容易超车的赛道之一，车队需要扩充他可用的动力单元部件储备。
这意味着这位积分榜领跑者在他的主场赛道上有着不同的任务：帮助他的队友、也是他最接近的争冠对手去争夺杆位。
这包括在拉塞尔的两次Q3飞驰圈中提供协助。安东内利在每圈开始时跑在队友前方，让他在大直道上获得尾流，然后再让拉塞尔通过。
Russell 最终从这一安排中获益，获得了发车榜第二位，仅次于 加斯利，后者夺得了自己的首个 F1 杆位。
“显然这是一种非常奇怪的感觉，”Antonelli 谈到他这个不同寻常的周六下午时说，“我必须完成我的任务，那就是帮助 George。我尽了最大努力来提供尽可能多的帮助。”
Antonelli 在第三节排位赛中唯一一次自己做出的尝试，是在该阶段中段一条几乎空旷的赛道上完成的。在给 Russell 提供尾流牵引后，他继续跑了一圈，做出了一个足以排在该节第七位的圈速。
他的排位赛名次最终并不重要，因为他将因超出动力单元部件允许配额的处罚而从发车榜末尾起步——这一点在周末开始前就已经是众所周知的事情了。
"Q3很奇怪，就连我跑的那一圈也是,"他说。"那是一圈不错的成绩，但没有什么特别的。我车里的油比平时要多。我不想犯任何会破坏我们既定计划的错误，也就是在最后一圈也要给George提供尾流。显然心情很复杂，但就是这样。我们已经准备好明天全力以赴。"
尽管两位梅赛德斯车手都参与了总冠军争夺，车队一直坚称Russell和Antonelli必须首先以车队利益为重，包括在需要时接受车队指令以最大化车队成绩。
安东内利，梅赛德斯，拉塞尔，梅赛德斯
两周前在赞德沃特，Russell正是这么做的。Antonelli原本跑在他前面，之后在虚拟安全车期间晚进站，这使他落到Russell身后，但他拥有更新的轮胎。梅赛德斯随后指示Russell让Antonelli通过，尽管他起初质疑这一指令，但还是照做了。
在蒙扎，轮到Antonelli为车队战术做出贡献了。由于Russell预计在本赛季晚些时候也需要更换额外的动力单元部件，Antonelli表示，如果机会出现，他希望队友能给予回报。
“我们在这件事上意见一致，”他说，“既然他在赞德沃特当过好队友，我也照车队的要求做了。我很高兴最终结果不错。
“当然，轮到他的时候，我们会再讨论。这一点我们很清楚。只要可以，我们就会互相帮助，尤其是在这种情况下。我当时没有什么可赢的，而他正在争夺杆位。”
由于Russell在积分榜上落后Antonelli 59分，而他的队友因受罚将退后发车，蒙扎为他提供了一个缩小差距的好机会。
然而，目前仍不清楚 Antonelli 是否会在今年晚些时候需要更换更多发动机部件，梅赛德斯正在研发升级版发动机。Russell 清除自己罚退的最佳机会可能是巴库，这是赛历上另一个被认为超车相对容易的赛道。
detailEn: "I did what the team asked": Kimi Antonelli expects George Russell to return favour later in season
With a grid penalty compromising his own Monza weekend, Kimi Antonelli focused on helping title rival George Russell in qualifying - and expects the favour to be returned
George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes
After helping George Russell with a tow in Monza qualifying, Kimi Antonelli says he expects his team-mate and championship rival to act in the same way later in the season.
The Italian had little to gain from his own qualifying result because of a back-of-the-grid penalty and effectively spent the session helping Russell, who ultimately qualified second.

Mercedes took the opportunity to install new engine components in Antonelli's car at Monza, given it is one of the easier tracks on the calendar for overtaking and the team needed to expand his pool of available power unit components.
It meant the championship leader had a different job at his home track: helping his team-mate and closest title rival in the fight for pole position.
That included assisting Russell on both of his Q3 runs. Antonelli ran ahead of his team-mate at the start of the laps to give him a slipstream down the main straight before letting Russell through.
Russell ultimately benefited from the arrangement and earned second place on the grid, behind Pierre Gasly, who claimed his maiden F1 pole position.
“Obviously it's a very weird feeling," Antonelli said of his unusual Saturday afternoon. "I had to do my job, which was to help George. I tried my best in order to help as much as possible."

Antonelli's only attempt of his own in Q3 came on an almost empty track in the middle of the session. Having given Russell a tow, he continued for another lap and posted a time good enough for seventh in the session.

His qualifying position ultimately mattered little, as he will start the race from the back of the grid because of his penalty for exceeding his permitted allocation of power unit components – something that was already known before the start of the weekend.

“Q3 was very weird, even the lap I did," he said. "It was an OK lap, but nothing special. I had more fuel in the car than what you normally would have. I didn't want to do any mistakes that would compromise the program that we had planned, which was to give the slipstream to George in the last lap as well. Obviously mixed feelings, but it's what it is. We're ready to fight tomorrow.”

Despite both Mercedes drivers being involved in the title fight, the team has been adamant that Russell and Antonelli must act in the team's interests first and foremost, including accepting team orders when required to maximise its result.
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes

Russell did exactly that two weeks ago at Zandvoort. Antonelli had been running ahead of him before making a late pit stop under the virtual safety car, which dropped him behind Russell but left him on fresher tyres. Mercedes subsequently instructed Russell to let Antonelli through, and he complied despite initially questioning the call.

At Monza, it was Antonelli's turn to play the team game. And with Russell also expected to need additional power unit components later in the season, Antonelli expects his team-mate to return the favour if the opportunity arises.
“We're all aligned on this," he said. "As he's been a good team player in Zandvoort, I did what the team asked me to do. I'm happy that it worked out.

“Of course, when it's his turn, we're going to talk about it. We're very clear on that. When we can, we will help each other, especially in this kind of situation. I had nothing to win and he was fighting for pole.”
With Russell trailing Antonelli in the championship by 59 points, Monza presents him with a good opportunity to close the gap because of his team-mate's penalty.

Yet it remains unclear whether Antonelli will need to take further engine components later in the year, with Mercedes working on an upgraded engine. The best opportunity for Russell to clear his own penalties could be Baku, another track on the calendar where overtaking is considered relatively easy.

items.originalTitle: 皮亚斯特里Q3失误令诺里斯损失“半秒”
items.summaryEn: Lando Norris believes he could have been about half a second faster on his final qualifying lap at Monza had team-mate Oscar Piastri not made a mistake in the closing moments of Italian GP qualifying, which may have cost him grid positions.
detailZh: 奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在意大利大奖赛排位赛Q3中的失误，如何让兰多·诺里斯损失了"半秒"圈速
兰多·诺里斯认为，如果不是队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里未能给他提供尾流，他在蒙扎最后一圈排位赛圈速可能快了大约"半秒"。
兰多·诺里斯相信，如果不是队友奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在意大利大奖赛排位赛的最后时刻出现失误，他本可以在蒙扎排位赛中做出更快的圈速，这可能实际上让这位卫冕F1世界冠军在发车格上损失了几个位置。
诺里斯在排位赛中名列第九，他Q3的最佳圈速来自第一次尝试。他的1分22.256秒让他在第一轮之后排在第七位，但在第二次尝试中他未能提升成绩。
他估计，这在很大程度上要归结于这样一个事实：在排位赛的最后阶段，他实际上成为了第一个上路的车辆。
诺里斯后来解释说，迈凯伦的计划是让皮亚斯特里在那一圈跑在他前面，为他提供尾流牵引。迈凯伦的车手们是最后阶段最先驶出维修区的，皮亚斯特里在诺里斯前面。但第一轮排在第三位的皮亚斯特里在1号弯出现失误，锁死了轮胎并放弃了那一圈，导致诺里斯失去了尾流的帮助，而在蒙扎这条赛道上尾流尤为重要。
第一轮时，诺里斯在皮亚斯特里前面，但仍然享受了前方乔治·拉塞尔的尾流。他的单圈时间比队友慢了百分之三秒，而第二轮时由于皮亚斯特里的失误，他失去了原计划的牵引配合。
"我在Q3第一轮有优先权，必须第一个驶出维修区，这意味着奥斯卡前面有几辆车，而我前面只有一辆（拉塞尔），我的时间损失主要都发生在直道上，"诺里斯说。
"所以这不是我能做什么的问题，那一圈也不是我最好的表现，我不打算否认这一点，但我大部分时间都损失在直道上——当然，第二次出场时，轮到我跟在别人后面获得一点尾流优势，而这一点显然没有像我期望的那样顺利。"
诺里斯解释说，由于迈凯伦仍在为直线速度而挣扎，他和他的队友需要特别紧密地跟随其他赛车，需要大约两秒的差距才能优化他们的飞驰圈。
事实上，当皮亚斯特里冲线开始他在排位赛中的最后一圈时，诺里斯仅在其后2.3秒跟进。但这位澳大利亚车手在1号弯入弯前右前轮锁死，驶上了逃生通道。等他重新回到赛道时，诺里斯已经驶来并超过了他的队友。
皮亚斯特里解释说，迈凯伦在维修通道中的位置——车队车库距离维修通道出口很远——是决定让赛车首先出场的原因。等待更久可能会导致两位车手排在队伍最后，并可能没有足够的时间完成他们的最后一圈。
“尾流显然非常重要，”这位澳大利亚车手说。“我们在进入这个练习时段之前就大概知道，鉴于我们在维修通道中的位置，我们经常必须第一个驶出车库，因为如果不这样做，我们最终就会排在最后。我们身后，也就是我和Lando的身后，相当混乱。
“而如果你出发得不够早，你就会被堵在最后面，跑不出计时圈。
皮亚斯特里还承认，他在尝试弥补时间损失时，在1号弯刹车时过于激进。
“所以第二圈，是的，我是领着车队在跑，”他说。“我想我进1号弯时已经慢了大约0.2秒。所以我试图弥补。刹车点会随着这种速度差异发生很大变化。所以我可能尝试得太激进了，锁死了前轮，就这样了。”
这使得诺里斯没有了拖车，他的第二圈成绩为1分22.573秒，比第一圈慢了大约十分之三。
当被问到尾流是否可能价值两到三个十分之一秒时，诺里斯坚持认为其价值要大得多：“不，更像是半秒，甚至可能更多。”
如果他最后一圈能提高半秒，诺里斯本有可能参与到与法拉利和马克斯·维斯塔潘的竞争中，他们在排位赛中占据第四到第六的位置。
“这让我付出了代价，因为我没有尾流，就是这样，”他说。“没关系，我们作为一辆车很没用，我们在直道上太慢了，我们必须有好的尾流，否则我们速度不够快。
“Oscar很好地利用了尾流，他能让它发挥作用。而我的机会始终没有出现，所以我只能认栽。”
由于安东内利的罚退，Norris仍然会上升一个位置，这意味着他将从第八位发车，这位意大利车手在本周末更换了新的动力单元部件后将从发车阵型的最后起步。
尽管如此，这位迈凯伦车手认为，由于他的赛车在直线速度上落后于对手，他从来没有真正参与过杆位的争夺。
“我认为这个周末最痛苦的事情就是直线速度的差距，”他说。“Kimi几乎不用借助尾流就能跑出22.1秒或22.0秒。如果有尾流，他就能跑出21.6秒左右的成绩。”
“我认为我们需要非常贴近前车来获得尾流牵引。我只有一个车的牵引，而Oscar有两个车的牵引（在第一圈），我因此慢了零点二秒。从这个角度来说很痛苦，但目前我们只能接受这个现实。”
在匈牙利和荷兰连续赢下最近两场比赛后，Norris清楚在蒙扎很难重复这样的成绩——不仅因为他的发车位置，还因为这条赛道对迈凯伦的赛车特性不太有利。
“那些快的人是因为他们真的快，不是因为运气好。从排位赛Q1的第一圈开始他们就很快，”他说。“他们快是因为他们在直道上很出色，低速弯也很好，他们完全配得上现在的位置，他们没有任何运气成分。”
“对我们来说，我们可能是直道上最慢的车队之一。我们必须在别人身后两秒开始一个飞驰圈，这非常疯狂。否则的话，我们根本不快。明天看看我们能做些什么吧，但我觉得在任何情况下，如果能跑到干净空气里，我们也不会有很好的表现。说实话，我觉得我们差得还挺远的。”
"只是奥斯卡今天做得很好，而我从来没有得到过那样的机会。"
皮亚斯特里最终在排位赛中排名第三，但由于在第二节排位赛中阻挡了Lawson，被处以退三位发车的处罚，周日他将从第六位发车。
detailEn: How Oscar Piastri's Q3 mistake denied Lando Norris "half a second" in Italian GP qualifying
Lando Norris reckons he may have been around "half a second" quicker on his final qualifying lap at Monza had his team-mate Oscar Piastri not failed to provide him with a tow

Lando Norris believes he could have set a quicker lap in Monza qualifying had his team-mate Oscar Piastri not made a mistake in the closing moments of Italian Grand Prix qualifying, which may effectively have cost the defending Formula 1 world champion a few positions on the grid.
Norris was ninth in qualifying, with his best Q3 lap coming on his first attempt. His 1m22.256s put him seventh in the order after the first runs, but he was unable to improve on his second attempt.
This was largely down to the fact that, he reckons, he ended up effectively first on the road in the closing stages of the session.

Norris later explained that McLaren's plan was for Piastri to run ahead of him on that attempt to provide him with a tow. The McLaren drivers were the first to leave the pits for the final runs, with Piastri leading Norris. But Piastri, who was third after the first runs, made a mistake into Turn 1, locked up and aborted his lap, leaving Norris without the assistance of a slipstream, which is particularly valuable at Monza.

On the first run, Norris had been ahead of Piastri but still had a slipstream from George Russell in front. His time was three tenths slower than his team-mate's, before he was left without the planned tow on the second run because of Piastri's mistake.

"I had priority in terms of I had to go out first of the pitlane on Q3 run one, which meant Oscar had a couple of cars ahead of him and I just had the one [of Russell] and most of my time loss is just in the straights," Norris said.

"So it's nothing I can do, it wasn't my best lap either, I'm not going to deny that, but the majority of my time is just lost in the straights - and of course on the second run, it's my time to go behind and get a bit of a slipstream and that certainly didn't go as I'd hoped."

Norris explained that because McLaren is still struggling with straightline speed, he and his team-mate needed to follow other cars particularly closely, with a gap of around two seconds required to optimise their laps.

Indeed, when Piastri crossed the line to start his final lap in qualifying, Norris followed just 2.3 seconds later. But the Australian locked his right-front tyre on the approach to Turn 1 and took to the escape road. By the time he rejoined the track, Norris was already coming through and passed his team-mate.

Piastri explained that McLaren's position in the pitlane, with the team's garage being far from pit exit, was behind the decision to send its cars out first. Waiting longer risked leaving both drivers at the back of the queue and potentially without enough time to complete their final laps.

“The slipstream is really important, obviously,“ the Australian said. “We kind of knew going into the into the session that where we are in the pitlane, we often have to leave the garage first, because if we don't, we end up being last. There was a fair bit of mess behind us, behind me and Lando.
“And if you don't go early enough, you get stuck right at the back of that and you don't get a lap.”
Piastri also admitted he had been too ambitious under braking for Turn 1 as he tried to make up time.

“So the second lap, yeah, I was leading the train around,“ he said. “I think I was already like two tenths down into Turn 1. So I tried to compensate. Your braking point changes quite a lot with that speed difference. So I tried to probably be a bit too ambitious, locked the front and that was it.”
That left Norris without a tow, and his second lap was a 1m22.573s, around three tenths slower than his first.
When asked whether a slipstream could be worth two or three tenths, Norris insisted its value was considerably greater: “No, it's more like half a second, maybe even more.”

An improvement of half a second on his final lap could potentially have put Norris in the fight with the Ferraris and Max Verstappen, who occupied positions from fourth to sixth in the qualifying order.

“It cost me because I have no slipstream, that's it," he said. “It doesn't matter, we're useless as a car, we're so slow in the straight, we have to have a good slipstream otherwise we're not quick enough.
“Oscar made use of a good slipstream and he could make it work. My chance never came around, so I just have to take it on the chin.”

Norris will still gain one position thanks to Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty, meaning he is set to start eighth, with the Italian dropping to the back of the grid after taking new power unit components this weekend.
Still, the McLaren driver believes he was never in the fight for pole because of his car's straightline speed deficit compared to the opposition.

“I think the most painful thing this weekend is just the straightline speed deficit," he said. "Kimi could do a 22.1s or a 22.0s pretty much with no slipstream. With a slipstream he [would be] doing a 21.6s or something.

“I think we needed to be incredibly close to someone. I had a one car tow and I lose two tenths to Oscar who had a two-car tow [on the first run]. It's painful in that sense, but otherwise it's just what we've got to live with for now.”

After winning the last two races in Hungary and the Netherlands, Norris is aware it will be difficult to repeat that result at Monza - not only because of his starting position, but because the track is less favourable to McLaren's characteristics.

"The people who were quick are because they're quick, not because they got lucky. They were quick from Q1 run one," he said. "They're quick because they're very good in the straights, they're good in low-speed corners, they completely deserve to be where they are, they didn't get lucky in any way.

"For us, we're probably one of the slowest in the straights. We have to start a lap two seconds behind someone, which is pretty insane. Otherwise, we're just not quick at all. We'll see what we can do tomorrow, but I think in any situation, if we get to [be in] clean air, we're not going to be very good at all. Really, I think we're quite a long way off.
"It's just that Oscar did a good job today and I never had that opportunity."
Piastri ended up third in qualifying, but will start Sunday's race from sixth after receiving a three-place grid penalty for impeding Lawson in Q2.

detailZh: 杰里米·克拉克森在皮埃尔·加斯利拿下意大利大奖赛杆位后向阿尔派 F1车队作出承诺
杰里米·克拉克森承诺，如果皮埃尔·加斯利将他在意大利大奖赛上出人意料的杆位转化为胜利，就送阿尔派整个F1车队一箱Hawkstone啤酒
前《Top Gear》和《The Grand Tour》主持人杰里米·克拉克森承诺，如果皮埃尔·加斯利赢得意大利大奖赛，将送给整个阿尔派 F1车队Hawkstone啤酒。
加斯利在周六蒙扎的排位赛中名列第一，为周日的比赛锁定了他的首个杆位。
克拉克森的 Diddly Squat 农场位于奇平诺顿，距离 阿尔派 车队的恩斯通总部很近，他很快对这一里程碑时刻作出了反应。这位《克拉克森的农场》节目主持人在 X 上发帖，向车队公开许下承诺。
“好了。加斯利。没有压力，但如果你把这个杆位转化为一场胜利，全队每人都能得到一份 Hawkstone。加油，奇平诺顿车队。”他发帖写道。
这延续了克拉克森公开支持他“本地”F1 车队的传统。在 2023 赛季，摩纳哥大奖赛期间他曾发推称，如果 奥康 登上领奖台，他就请整个 阿尔派 车队喝一品脱啤酒。当 Ocon 成功获得第三名后，克拉克森兑现了承诺。他亲自开着他的兰博基尼拖拉机前往恩斯通工厂，为员工送去了一拖车足足 1000 瓶他自产的 Hawkstone 啤酒。
Gasly 在蒙扎的表现令本赛到目前为止一直由梅赛德斯主导的局面感到震惊，而蒙扎正是他 2020 年为 AlphaTauri 车队赢得职业生涯首个大奖赛冠军的同一条赛道。
“我收获了很多情感，所以我为整个车队感到无比高兴。我对我们的表现感到极其满意。我在F1已经九年了，每个周末都在竭尽全力，”加斯利在排位赛后的新闻发布会上解释道。
“并不是每次我们都能有一辆车去争夺杆位，而今天就是这样的情况。我真的非常、非常高兴，也非常自豪能够抓住这个机会并把它变为现实。那是一个了不起的一圈。
“从Q1的第一圈开始我们就一直处于状态。感觉一直很好。我在蒙扎这里获得了我的首胜，现在我又拿到了我的首个杆位，所以这里对我来说绝对是一个特别的地方。”
detailEn: Jeremy Clarkson makes Alpine F1 promise after Pierre Gasly Italian GP pole
Jeremy Clarkson has promised Alpine’s entire F1 team a Hawkstone beer if Pierre Gasly converts his surprise Italian GP pole position into victory
Former Top Gear and The Grand Tour host Jeremy Clarkson has promised the whole Alpine Formula 1 team a Hawkstone beer if Pierre Gasly wins the Italian Grand Prix.
Gasly topped Saturday's qualifying session at Monza, securing his maiden pole position for Sunday's race.

Clarkson, whose Diddly Squat Farm in Chipping Norton is situated close to Alpine's Enstone headquarters, quickly reacted to the milestone moment. Posting on X, the Clarkson's Farm presenter made a public promise to the team.
"Right. Pierre Gasly. No pressure but if you translate that pole into a win, the whole team gets a Hawkstone. Go Chipping Norton team," he posted.

It continues a trend of Clarkson publicly backing his "local" F1 team. In the 2023 season, he tweeted during the Monaco Grand Prix that he would buy the entire Alpine team a pint if Esteban Ocon secured a podium finish. When Ocon successfully finished third, Clarkson honoured his end of the bargain. He personally drove his Lamborghini tractor to the Enstone factory, delivering a trailer laden with 1000 bottles of his Hawkstone beer to the staff.
Gasly's performance at Monza, the same circuit where he claimed his maiden grand prix victory for AlphaTauri in 2020, came as a shock in a season that has so far been dominated by Mercedes.

"I acquired a lot of emotions, so I'm just extremely happy for the whole team. I'm extremely happy with our performance. It's been nine years I'm in Formula 1, trying to give my best absolutely every single weekend," Gasly explained in the post-qualifying press conference.
"It's not every time we get a car to fight for pole position, and today it was the case. I'm really, really happy, really proud to have seized this chance and make it work. It was a heck of a lap.
"We've been on it since the first lap in Q1. It's been feeling good. I got my first win here in Monza, and now I get my first pole position, so definitely a special place to me."

items.titleZh: 2026年F1意大利大奖赛排位赛赢家与输家
items.summaryZh: 意大利大奖赛排位赛诞生了十多年来F1最令人意外的干地杆位获得者，但除了他之外，围场中鲜有车手和车队对结果感到满意。
items.originalTitle: 2026年F1意大利大奖赛排位赛赢家与输家
items.summaryEn: Italian Grand Prix qualifying produced Formula 1's most surprising dry-weather polesitter in over a decade, but apart from him there were few in the pitlane with reasons to be cheerful.
detailZh: 意大利大奖赛排位赛诞生了十多年来F1干地条件下最令人意外的杆位得主。
但除了他之外，围场里没有多少人有值得高兴的理由。
领奖台价值15分，而杆位“一文不值”——皮埃尔·加斯利(加斯利)在这个周末内收获了一个杆位、失去了一个领奖台，但失去这15分对他F1履历而言似乎是一笔可以接受的交易。
他现在既是F1的分站冠军，也是F1的杆位得主。这感觉很对，也很有分量。无论周日结果如何，他都是F1历史记录中的第109位杆位得主。
但这对阿尔派来说也是一件大事——本赛季大部分时间里这支车队感觉有点像无人区，但似乎正从它的赞德沃特升级包中榨出一些不错的成果。
"我不认为我们在赞德沃特完全发挥出了这套升级包的最佳水平。那是一条有点古怪的赛道。但我们来到这里后，赛车表现非常出色，"阿尔派的董事总经理Steve Nielsen欣喜地对Sky说道。
"我们把间隙时机掌握对了，拖车也用对了。车手们没有犯错。而且圈速显然就在赛车里。因为两辆车都相当快。"
这不是第一辆在低下压力赛道上大放异彩的中游赛车，也不会是最后一辆，但与整个赛季的其他比赛相比，这一次显得比平时更加重要。—— Val Khorounzhiy
“这辆车是纸做的，”马克斯·维斯塔潘在Q3通过无线电发出了一条奇怪的信息，因为红牛赛车持续出现一些虽小但代价高昂的损坏，这次是一个影响其离地高度的问题。对于这条弯上路肩很多的赛道来说，这并不理想。
当利亚姆·劳森在Q2中因遇到缓慢行驶的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里而被淘汰时，他认为这比失去尾流伙伴要重要得多。
输家：奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里（排位第三但被处罚）
单看纯粹的排位赛成绩，皮亚斯特里本可算作“赢家”类别的候选。他在一条不太适合阻力较大的迈凯伦的赛道上拿到了发车格第三位，遥遥领先于队友兰多·诺里斯，而且这一切尽管——但也在某种程度上正因为——他在最后一个计时圈冲过第一个减速弯时毁掉了那一圈。
但早在那时，处罚就已经极有可能了，因为皮亚斯特里在Q2第一个减速弯中间无意中但严重地阻挡了劳森。而且，如上文所述，那次Q3的失误毁掉了那个他本应为诺里斯提供有利拖车的飞驰圈。
所以随着第三位发车变成第六位，这个失误加上打乱了车队的计划，意味着皮亚斯特里最终登上了输家榜单。——MB
考虑到这位积分榜领跑者在蒙扎整个排位赛期间都充当队友拉塞尔的拖车仆人，通过一个没有拖车、不合时序且无关紧要的单独飞驰圈取得第七名，已经相当了不起了。
而且这可能表明：a) 如果他正常参加排位赛，他本可以毫无悬念地拿下杆位；b) 即使从周日发车格的最后一位起步，他也有机会取得非常、非常好的成绩。
他的一个争冠对手被一辆阿尔派抢走杆位，另一个仅排第五、落后于队友，并已暗示法拉利车队内部优先安排的矛盾——在本周末安东内利毫无压力的情况下，这对他来说相当有利。- MB
红牛曾希望用劳森（Lawson）在Q3为维斯塔潘（Verstappen）提供牵引——正如我们现在所知，劳森面临着排到最后发车的引擎处罚。"但显然你得先进入Q3才能做到这一点，"劳森在Q2被淘汰、位列第14后反思道。
这比他在比赛中通过无线电表达的情绪平静多了。"伙计，搞什么鬼？"当他在第一个减速弯被皮亚斯特里（Piastri）阻挡时，他如此喊道——这一阻挡让这位迈凯伦车手吃到了发车处罚——随后在Q2结束时他对红牛说："兄弟，这真的太糟糕了。我不敢相信你们就这样把我他妈的晾在那里！"
也许皮亚斯特里的阻挡正是阻止他晋级的原因。也许不是；劳森最终慢了三分之十秒，最后一个计时段没有提升，整体表现徘徊在及格线上——而这也没能得益于他"在最后一圈之前整个排位赛都跑在干净气流中"这一事实。
“那是我第一次坐在一辆赛车后面，而且轮胎非常烫，”他说。“这本来就不是一个理想的情况，所以第一次就尝试这样做并不理想。不过我认为显然皮亚斯特里（Oscar）在一号弯的那一下可能比什么都更伤。”
无论原因是什么，劳森（Lawson）真的本应该进入排位赛的最后一节。——杰克·科曾斯（Jack Cozens）
在过去的四个月里不断倒退之后，哈斯（哈斯）车队需要它在蒙扎带来的升级能展现出一些令人鼓舞的东西。
因此，贝尔曼（Bearman）称其“天壤之别”，并且在他取得自三月上海站以来最佳排位赛成绩的同时，感到自己有机会进入Q3，这样的表现已经相当不错了。
Bearman 比队友 奥康 快了七分之七秒（0.7秒）。只有 Bearman 用上了升级版法拉利引擎，但他认为这只是很微小的差异，并表示如果这是蒙扎赛道上赛车唯一的改动，他仍然要为摆脱Q1而挣扎。
Ocon 拥有同样的空气动力学升级。当被问到这些升级是否有效时，他回答说：“它们在 Ollie 那边有效果。” - MB
Tsunoda 在直道上损失了大量圈速，并且听起来对此完全感到困惑，他的这番话对任何人来说都不会陌生，因为2026年整个围场里，车手们都在谈论单圈的动力部署、优化之类的话题。
“我是说，看第一个计时段，我慢了大约0.7秒——而那里只有两个弯角，”他沉思道。“我不觉得自己犯了什么重大错误，以至于在基本上是直线的地方损失了这么多圈速。”
“我在练习赛里经历过很多状况，但从来没发生过这样的事。”
他的发车位置其实并不算太糟——不过，鉴于这一切显然是他向未来的F1潜在雇主证明自身价值任务的一部分，他很不走运，这次注定短暂的替补出场竟然包括一条像这样能量匮乏的赛道，无论是缺乏对这些赛车特性的经验，还是碰上了罕见的动能部署问题，或者两者兼有，都可能真正、真正地造成严重伤害。——VK
“看起来我们的运行状态好多了。一切都在正常运转。就像我说的，当你能真正用一辆状态正常的车跑圈时，找到节奏也变得容易得多。”
博塔斯谈的是到目前为止本周末他这一侧凯迪拉克车库的执行情况——“基本上没出过一个问题”——但他的话其实也完全适用于他这个赛季的整体局面。
在排位赛中，他已经对队友塞尔吉奥·佩雷兹（Sergio Perez）取得了6比0的连胜——这是一个显著的逆转，因为赛季初他在纸面上表现足够挣扎，以至于人们开始讨论2027年可能的替代人选。
佩雷兹在Q1遇到了一些问题，也没有得到他想要的尾流牵引——但他也承认博塔斯（Bottas）做出了强劲的表现，自己"无法匹敌"。
至于明天，两人都仍需挺过开局阶段——博塔斯担心刹车在车流中跟车时如何应对——不过尽管凯迪拉克仍在经历这些初期的磨合问题，局势对博塔斯来说肯定是在朝好的方向发展。——VB
在前两站带来了有节制的乐观之后，意大利大奖赛的这个周末到目前为止对阿斯顿·马丁-本田来说是一次残酷的现实检验。
好吧，如果费尔南多·阿隆索（阿隆索）在Q1能出来跑第二轮的话，他可能本可以排在这两台凯迪拉克之前（因此也可能超过亚历克斯·阿尔本/阿尔本的威廉姆斯）。阿隆索显然觉得还有圈速可以挖掘。
“我们只跑了一套轮胎，而我们做出的成绩是用一套已经用过的轮胎完成的，之前在维修区等了很长时间，轮胎是冷的等等，”他说。“所以我认为最后一趟尝试应该还能有更好的成绩。”
但他为什么没能利用这个机会，还得在Q1结束前提前下车呢？“引擎启动不了，所以我们的动力单元出了问题。我不知道是内燃机的动力问题，还是电池问题，还是别的什么，总之，它启动不了。”
周日下午可能会很漫长、很孤独。—— JC
detailEn: Italian Grand Prix qualifying produced Formula 1’s most surprising dry weather polesitter in over a decade.
But apart from him, there weren’t many in the pitlane with reasons to be cheerful.

A podium is worth 15 points and a pole is worth 'nothing' - Pierre Gasly has gained a pole and lost a podium in the span of this weekend, and yet it feels like the loss of 15 points is an acceptable trade for his F1 CV.
He's now an F1 winner and an F1 polesitter. That feels right. That feels significant. Regardless of what Sunday brings, he's poleman number 109 in F1's history books.
But it's also a big deal for Alpine, which has felt a bit no man's land-y for much of this season but seems to be squeezing out some good juice from its Zandvoort upgrade.

"I don't think we quite got the best out of the package in Zandvoort. It's a bit of a quirky circuit. But we've come here and the car is responding very well," an elated Steve Nielsen, Alpine's managing director, told Sky.
"We got the gaps right. We got the tows right. The drivers didn't make a mistake. And laptime's clearly in the car. Because both cars were quite quick."

It's not the first midfield car to star on a low-downforce track, and it won't be the last, but compared to the rest of the season it feels even more significant than it usually would. - Val Khorounzhiy

"This car is made out of paper," was a curious Q3 radio message from Max Verstappen, as the Red Bull’s habit of small but costly breakages continued with a problem that affected its ride height. Not ideal for this kerb-heavy circuit.
He felt that was far more significant than losing his slipstream wingman when Liam Lawson was eliminated in Q2 after coming across the slow-moving Oscar Piastri.
Loser: Oscar Piastri (3rd but penalised)

On pure qualifying results, Piastri was a ‘winner’ category candidate. Third on the grid at a track not great for the draggy McLaren, a long way ahead of team-mate Lando Norris and all despite (but also partly because of) blowing his last qualifying lap with a trip over the first chicane.

But already by that time a penalty was highly likely given Piastri’s inadvertent but massive block on Lawson in the middle of the first chicane in Q2. And, as referenced above, that Q3 error blew the lap on which he was supposed to be giving Norris a helpful tow.
So as third on the grid becomes sixth, that error and messing up the team’s plans means Piastri ends up in the Loser list instead. - MB

Given the championship leader spent all of Monza qualifying as team-mate Russell's tow servant, seventh in the actual results via one tow-less out of sequence solo lap that didn't matter was quite an achievement.

And one that probably suggests a) he'd have been a clear polesitter if he'd participated in qualifying properly and b) he has a shot at a very, very good result even from the back of the grid on Sunday.

One of his title rivals being beaten to pole by an Alpine and the other only qualifying fifth behind his team-mate and hinting at Ferrari team prioritisation angst already is quite good for Antonelli too on a weekend where he has nothing to lose. - MB

Red Bull hoped to use Lawson, faced as we now know with back-of-the-grid engine penalties, to tow Verstappen around in Q3. "But obviously you need to get there to be able to do it," reflected Lawson after his elimination, in 14th, in Q2.

That was much calmer than he'd been on the radio during the session. "Dude, what the f***?" he exclaimed as he was baulked by Piastri at the first chicane, which earned the McLaren driver a grid penalty, before telling Red Bull at the end of Q2: "Bro, that's actually appalling. I can't believe how badly you just left me out to f***ing dry!"

Maybe the Piastri block is what stopped him progressing. Maybe it wasn't; Lawson was three tenths away in the end, didn't improve in the final sector, and generally looked borderline - not helped by the fact he'd "spent the whole quali in clean air until that last lap".

"It was the first time I'd sat behind a car and the tyres were super hot," he said. "It just wasn't an ideal situation, so trying to do it for the first time was not ideal. But I think obviously having Oscar in Turn 1 probably hurt more than anything."
Whatever the cause(s), Lawson should really have been in the final part of qualifying. - Jack Cozens
Having spent the last four months sliding backwards, Haas needed the upgrade it brought to Monza to show something encouraging.
So for Bearman to declare it "night-and-day different" and feel he had a shot at Q3 as he produced his best qualifying result since Shanghai in March will do nicely.

Bearman was also seven tenths of a second faster than team-mate Esteban Ocon. Only Bearman has the upgraded Ferrari engine, but he felt that was only a marginal difference and that he'd still have been fighting to get out of Q1 if that was the only change on the car for Monza.
Ocon has the same aero upgrades. Asked if they worked, he replied: "They worked on Ollie’s side". - MB

Tsunoda lost a lot of laptime on the straights and sounded totally bewildered by it, in comments that will sound familiar to anyone who's heard drivers up and down the grid speak about single-lap deployment and optimisation and all that jazz across 2026.

"I mean, if you look at the first sector, I was like seven tenths off - and there's only two corners," he mused. "I don't think I've done anything massively wrong, enough to lose a lot of laptime a lot in basically a straight line.
"I've done a lot of things in practice and it didn't happen like this."

His grid position is far from horrific - but, given that all of this is obviously part of a mission to prove his value to prospective F1 employers down the line, he's unlucky that what will surely be a short stand-in stint includes an energy-starved track like this, whether either a lack of experience with these cars' quirks or a freak deployment issue or both can really, really bite. - VK
"It seems like we're on a better run. Things are working as they should. Like I said, it's also easy to find the rhythm when you can actually get laps with a car that works."
Bottas was talking about the execution of the weekend so far for his side of the Cadillac garage - "not really a single issue" - but his comments may as well apply to the wider picture of his season.

He's on a 6-0 run versus team-mate Sergio Perez in qualifyings, a significant reversal after a start to the season shaky enough on paper to where people started talking about potential replacements for 2027.
Perez had some issues through Q1 and didn't get the tow he would've liked - but also acknowledged Bottas put in a strong effort he "couldn't match".

For tomorrow, both still need to get through the opening stint - with Bottas worried about how the brakes will cope with running in traffic - but amid those continued teething problems for Cadillac things have certainly trended right for Bottas. - VB
After the measured optimism the previous two rounds have offered, the Italian GP weekend has been a bruising reality check for Aston Martin-Honda so far.

OK, Fernando Alonso might've outqualified the two Cadillacs (and therefore possibly Alex Albon's Williams) had he made it out for a second run in Q1. Alonso certainly felt there was more laptime to come.

"We only did one set of tyres and the time we set was done with a scrubbed set, after waiting on the pitlane for a long time, cold tyres, etc.," he said. "So I think there was something more to come on the last attempt."

But the reason he didn't get to exploit it, and had to hop out of the car early before Q1 had ended? "The engine didn't start, so we had a problem with the power unit. I don't know if it's the ICE power or the battery or whatever it is, but yeah, it didn't start."
Sunday could be a long, lonely afternoon. - JC

items.summaryEn: George Russell was frustrated with Max Verstappen "slamming on the brakes" at the start of their final Q3 laps in Italian Grand Prix qualifying, as the Mercedes driver narrowly missed out on pole.
detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔对马克斯·维斯塔潘在排位赛中的举动感到沮丧：“他直接猛踩了刹车”
在F1意大利大奖赛上，基米·安东内利本打算为乔治·拉塞尔提供尾流，马克斯·维斯塔潘却打乱了梅赛德斯的排位赛计划
在F1意大利大奖赛排位赛Q3的最后一圈开始时，马克斯·维斯塔潘“猛踩刹车”，令乔治·拉塞尔感到沮丧，这位梅赛德斯车手以微弱差距与杆位失之交臂。
在进入决定性的排位赛飞驰圈之前，维斯塔潘领先于基米·安东内利和拉塞尔组成的车队，后两人原本计划配合，为拉塞尔提供尽可能好的尾流，反正安东内利无论如何都要接受发车处罚。
不过，尽管安东内利和拉塞尔起初与红牛赛车之间还有一段健康的缓冲距离，但在他们出站圈的尾声——在帕拉波利卡弯前的直道末端——当维斯塔潘以极慢的速度驶向蒙扎的最后一个弯时，三辆赛车挤在了一起。维斯塔潘正好在安东内利前方加速，导致他和拉塞尔之间的距离太近，意大利人无法给他的梅赛德斯队友提供拖曳气流。
安东内利索性驶离赛道放弃了那个飞驰圈，而拉塞尔也觉得自己离这位荷兰车手太近，无法跑出最优的排位圈。
“维斯塔潘进入飞驰圈的时候，我们这边有点乱了，”拉塞尔怒气冲冲地说，他把杆位拱手让给了阿尔派的皮埃尔·加斯利。“本来一切都看起来很正常，但进入帕拉波利卡弯时，马克斯突然猛踩刹车，他不想当头车。”
“这就是那种你没法控制别人行为的事情之一。基米本来是要给我尾流的，第一次尝试时他做得非常完美。但显然碰上马克斯的情况，我觉得这也让基米很难判断该怎么办。所以只能说有点不走运。”
"我做飞驰圈时比Max慢了一秒半，这并不理想。"
Verstappen承认他也想借助Antonelli的尾流，在蒙扎这很容易决定是拿杆位还是排在第一排之外。但这位四届世界冠军表示，他在准备飞驰圈时遇到了动力单元故障，当他踩油门时发动机出现了顿挫。
当被问及是否想迫使Antonelli让路时，他回答说："是的，但我当时也正想加速，然后发动机熄火了。我要同时应对太多事情，这非常复杂。"
但梅赛德斯车队领队Toto Wolff表示，毫无疑问Verstappen在玩"聪明的"把戏。
"当然，Max 做得非常聪明，他让所有人在最后一个弯道前都挤在一起," Wolff 告诉 Sky Germany。"这意味着 Kimi 距离太近，让 George 无法获得良好的尾流效果，而 George 整圈都处在距离 Max 两秒以内。尤其是在 Parabolica 弯，他吃了亏，因为他只是紧咬在 Max 的车尾后面。"
Verstappen 最终获得第六名，但由于 皮亚斯特里 因阻挡 Verstappen 的队友 劳森 而受到发车处罚，他在周日的发车顺序上将上升一位。
detailEn: George Russell frustrated with Max Verstappen qualifying antics: "He just slammed on the brakes"
Max Verstappen disrupted Mercedes' qualifying plans at Formula 1's Italian Grand Prix as Kimi Antonelli aimed to give George Russell a slipstream

George Russell was frustrated with Max Verstappen "slamming on the brakes" at the start of their final Q3 laps in Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix qualifying as the Mercedes driver narrowly missed out on pole.

Heading into the decisive qualifying run, Verstappen was leading a train with Kimi Antonelli and Russell, who were planning to work together to hand Russell the best possible slipstream as Antonelli was facing a grid penalty anyway.

But while Antonelli and Russell initially had a healthy buffer to the Red Bull car, towards the end of their out-laps - on the back straight before the Parabolica corner - the three cars were bunched up when Verstappen drove extremely slowly towards Monza's final corner. Verstappen accelerated right ahead of Antonelli, ensuring he and Russell were too close together for the Italian to give his Mercedes team-mate a tow.
Antonelli peeled off and abandoned his lap instead, while Russell also felt he was too close to the Dutchman to turn an optimal qualifying lap.

"We had a bit of a mess with Verstappen entering the lap," Russell fumed as he lost pole to Alpine's Pierre Gasly. "Everything was all looking fine but then going into Parabolica, Max just slammed on the brakes and he didn't want to be the lead car.

"It's just one of those things, you can't control what other people do. Kimi was there to give me the slipstream, which he did perfectly on the first run. But obviously with Max, I think it also made it difficult for Kimi to know what to do as well. So it was just a little bit unfortunate.
"I did my lap a second and a half behind Max, which wasn't ideal."

Verstappen acknowledged that he wanted to pick up a slipstream from Antonelli as well, which can easily make the difference between pole and qualifying off the front row in Monza. But the four-time world champion said he faced power unit trouble as he prepared for his flying lap, with his engine stuttering as he revved it up.
When asked if he wanted to force Antonelli past, he replied: "Yeah, but I was also trying to accelerate and then the engine cut out. I had so many things going on, it's super complicated."
But Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff there was no doubt Verstappen was playing "clever" games.

"Max, of course, did it very cleverly, he made everyone bunch up before the last corner," Wolff told Sky Germany. "That meant Kimi was too close for a good slipstream for George, and George then spent the whole lap within two seconds of Max. Especially in the Parabolica, he lost out because he was simply hanging on Max's gearbox."
Verstappen ended up in sixth, but will gain a place on Sunday's starting grid following Oscar Piastri's grid penalty for impeding Verstappen's team-mate Liam Lawson.

Pierre Gasly felt he was "robbed" on Friday after losing his podium from June's Monaco Grand Prix but turned it around in the most remarkable fashion with pole position for the Italian Grand Prix.
Just one day after the FIA International Court of Appeal reinstated Gasly's pit lane speeding penalties, the Alpine driver hit back with his maiden Formula 1 pole.

Did 'extra motivation' power Gasly to pole?

Gasly has always shown plenty of emotion in and out of the car but was furious after finding out McLaren and Red Bull's appeals of the Monaco race result led to the return of his two five-second time penalties for speeding.
In June, Alpine had successfully won a right of review that saw the penalties removed as they proved Gasly was not speeding due to an incorrect measurement of the pit lane distance.

Gasly told Canal+ that "we're being robbed" and "I don't think this is going to end here" while Alpine chief Flavio Briatore questioned the relationship between the reigning constructors' champions and a judge at the FIA's International Court of Appeal (ICA).
The ICA responded to Briatore's comments on Saturday and stated they are "confident in the soundness of the proceedings and the integrity of the judges".

McLaren's Team Principal Andrea Stella was not happy with Flavio Briatore's reaction to the ruling which meant Alpine's Pierre Gasly lost his Monaco GP third place finish after his two time penalties were reapplied
Nevertheless it certainly fired Gasly up and he produced one of the best laps in his nine-year F1 career, admitting the situation regarding the appeal was "not nice" but something he tried to use.
"I try to use everything I can into something positive and, extra motivation, but I think I could have dealt without it this weekend. That's all I'll say," he said.

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen added to Sky Sports F1: "When you think what the mood was in the camp when we got the result from Monaco, which honestly is going to annoy me for the rest of my life, it's a nice way to bounce back with pole position. It's lovely."

Several drivers congratulated Gasly on his pole, including George Russell who will start on the front row in Sunday's race.
Russell revealed he was playing chess with Gasly before qualifying and the Alpine driver also beat him in their game.

"We were actually finishing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there, and I thought, 'Well, I think I'll beat you in qualifying,' and here we are, he's ahead of me again," he said.
"So, yeah, huge congrats to him. Pierre and Alpine have been super-fast even from Q1."

Gasly's only win so far in F1 came at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix - one year after his close friend Anthoine Hubert died and now he has another unexpected chance for a second victory.
The Alpine has been very quick in the straights in Monza thanks to the benefit of a Mercedes power unit, but the team also have a low-drag car which is strong aerodynamically.
Monza is an energy-rich track, so there is expected to be different power unit deployment strategies at play which will lead to the yoyo style of racing we saw earlier this year.
It may give Gasly a chance to keep Russell behind, or stick with him if the Mercedes driver is ahead.

detailEn: F1 fans celebrate Pierre Gasly after "insane" Italian GP pole position
Pierre Gasly claimed his first Formula 1 pole position at Monza
Alpine's Pierre Gasly secured his first career pole position at the Italian Grand Prix, beating Mercedes driver George Russell to the top spot by just 0.060 seconds at Monza.
In the first year of the new 2026 technical regulations, the season has largely been dictated by the frontrunning Mercedes pairing of Russell and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Gasly's result at Monza drew immediate and overwhelming support across social media. Fans celebrated the milestone moment for the Frenchman, who claimed his maiden grand prix victory at the same circuit in 2020.
"I cannot believe it. No red flags, no crashes, no penalties. Just straight-up faster than everyone else. Allez Gasly!" one fan commented on Reddit, while another added: "Liked by Pierre Gasly."

"I didn't think I could be so happy for someone outside of my team (Ferrari). That was just an insane lap he pulled together. Congrats Pierre," another comment read, and someone else posted: "I'm not even an Alpine fan this season but OMG that was peak performance from Gasly. If he wins tomorrow, that would be historic."

The pole position came after Gasly lost his third-place finish at the Monaco Grand Prix following an FIA International Court of Appeal ruling. "Lose P3 Monaco. Win Monza pole. WORTH IT," one fan commented, while another added: "Gasly heard his podium was taken from him and decided to get another one."
Someone else posted: "What a way to prove himself after losing a podium in Monaco. Happy for him."

Further reactions included: "Tomorrow we are all Alpine fans. Pierre Gasly, you took that rescinded podium personally," and "He's been quietly consistent for years now even though the Alpine is average. If they put him back in any of the fast cars, I think he'd give any one of the drivers a run for their money."

"我一出去跑排位赛，赛车上又有什么东西出故障了,"维斯塔潘对天空体育F1表示。
"这个问题我们是知道的，今年已经发生过好几次了，但它在低速路段就是很损失圈速，赛车跳动得比应该的程度厉害得多。在颠簸路面上、在路肩上，赛车已经不再有好的顺应性了。

这位四届世界冠军在排位赛中排名第六，但由于皮亚斯特里因阻挡他人被处以发车位处罚，他将上升一位至第五位发车。

detailEn: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff blames Max Verstappen for George Russell missing out on Italian GP pole to Pierre Gasly

George Russell missed out on pole as Pierre Gasly claimed a shock result for Alpine; Russell's final qualifying lap appeared to be compromised by Max Verstappen; watch the Italian Grand Prix live on Sunday at 2pm on Sky Sports F1, with build-up from 12.30pm
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Italian Grand Prix

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has claimed that George Russell missed out on pole position for the Italian Grand Prix because he "got done over" by Max Verstappen during the closing stages of qualifying at Monza.

Russell appeared to be on course to live up to his status as pole favourite, but his final flying lap was compromised by Red Bull's Verstappen slowing down in front of him and his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Mercedes had placed championship leader Antonelli on track in front of Russell to give the Brit a tow, due to the fact the Italian is serving penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance for the season and was going to start the race from the back of the grid regardless of his qualifying position.

Russell still improved his time to go fastest but then had pole remarkably snatched away from him by Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who pulled off one of the biggest qualifying shocks in the sport's history.
Pierre Gasly claims Alpine's first pole in 17 years!
Asked by Sky Sports F1 whether something had gone wrong for Russell to miss out on pole, Wolff said: "Yeah, I think at the end where he got done over by Max in the final run when launching the lap.
"It was just much too close, and that compromised the lap time eventually and that lost pole position."
With having a tow from the car in front being crucial to delivering a fast lap at Monza, Verstappen sought to force another car in front after having lost touch with the McLarens ahead of him.
As Verstappen slowed down ahead of the final corner, Antonelli passed the Red Bull, while Russell remained just behind them.
While a tow is useful, being too close to the car in front for the entire lap can also have a negative impact on performance, which Russell felt was the case.
Mercedes driver George Russell reacts to narrowly missing out on pole position to Pierre Gasly during qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix
"We had a bit of a mess with Verstappen entering the lap," Russell said. "He wanted to go for the tow, Kimi was there as well, and I did my lap a second and a half behind Max, which wasn't ideal.

Asked whether Mercedes could have done anything differently to avoid the situation, Russell replied: "I think, no, everything was all looking fine, but then going into Parabolica, Max just slammed on the brakes, and he didn't want to be the lead car.

"So, it's just one of those things. You can't control what other people do. Kimi was there to give me the slipstream, which he did perfectly on the first run, but obviously with Max, I think it also made it difficult for Kimi to know what to do as well.
"So, it was just a little bit unfortunate. In hindsight, probably would have been better off not trying this, but we wanted to give it everything."
Pierre Gasly reacts to a shock first pole position at Italian GP
Despite his frustration at missing out on pole, Russell remains in with a strong chance of reducing his 59-point deficit to Antonelli at the top of the standings.
He told Sky Sports F1: "I'm feeling good. I think the key is just to have a clean start, a clean first lap.
"As long as I'm in the top three or four after the first few laps, you're still within a great shot to fight for victory. That's the goal."
Verstappen: My car was jumping like a kangaroo
Verstappen didn't address the final-corner incident after qualifying, but revealed his own pace had been compromised by damage to his car, causing it to jump "like a kangaroo".
"As soon as I went out for qualifying, something failed again on the car," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1.

"It's something that we are aware of, and it happens more often in the year, but it's just costing lap time in the low-speed where the car just starts jumping around a lot more than it should do. On the bumps, the kerbs, the car's not compliant anymore.

"I was actually very happy with the car in FP3 because we took a big step forward from yesterday. The car was in a much better window, and overall I think today it was in a much better window, and overall I think today it was in a much better window.
"But when you have no ride control and the car is just jumping around like a kangaroo, you can't be consistent. It's actually a bit of a shame to not optimise our performance.
The four-time world champion qualified sixth but will move up a place to fifth on the grid due to Oscar Piastri being given a grid penalty for impeding.
On his prospects for the race, he added: "We need to be able to change whatever the part is, because otherwise it's going to be quite tough to race like that."

detailZh: 意大利大奖赛排位赛爆出大冷门，皮埃尔·加斯利和阿尔派击败乔治·拉塞尔和梅赛德斯（以及其他F1领先车手），夺得杆位。
但在第三节排位赛结束时，发车顺位尚未完全确定，因为基米·安东内利、亚历克斯·阿尔本和利亚姆·劳森因更换引擎部件被处以三个发车位置罚退。
此外还有一处变动：排位赛第三名的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里因在第二节排位赛中阻挡劳森，被罚退三个发车位置。
周日早上，红牛和阿斯顿·马丁分别让劳森和阿隆索违反赛后封存规定，从维修区发车。
对于Lawson来说，这是为了更换一套新的尾翼组件，而在Alonso那边，阿斯顿·马丁更换了Honda的发动机部件——即MGU-K、控制电子设备和能量储存单元。
**因更换发动机部件而受后排发车处罚
detailEn: Italian Grand Prix qualifying threw up a real shock as Pierre Gasly and Alpine beat George Russell and Mercedes (and the rest of the Formula 1 frontrunners) to pole position.
But the starting grid wasn't quite set in stone come the end of Q3, as three grid penalties for engine component changes - for Kimi Antonelli, Alex Albon and Liam Lawson - were applied.
And there was a further change, too, as third-place qualifier Oscar Piastri received a three-place grid drop for impeding Lawson in Q2.
On Sunday morning, Red Bull and Aston Martin then committed to pitlane starts for Lawson and Fernando Alonso respectively, by breaching parc ferme.
For Lawson, this was to fit a new rear wing assembly, while on Alonso' side Aston Martin replaced Honda engine components - namely the MGU-K, the control electronics and the energy store.
